items.title: Politics is upon us
items.description: IT wasn’t an ordinary day by any stretch of the imagination, even though it began rather ordinarily. There was little news to interest anyone (and Kashmir was a no-no for television channels). Initially, there came fleeting news about a press conference by the head of ISPR but it wasn’t meant to be. Those who had not been invited to the event thought the news was incorrect but later it transpired that the conference had been delayed to the next day, Friday. And then came the bombshell — in Islamabad at an event hosting businessmen for a conference on the economy, business and all things complicated. Here, instead of the speeches by the men managing Pakistan’s finances (if there were any), it was Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s speech that got all the attention. It’s still not clear why he spoke there but as the conference took place at a hall located close to his office, perhaps he offered to swing by and say a few words. His speech didn’t just create headlines; it created an entire news cycle. In simple words, he confirmed in a way what the government’s worst critics have been saying — that people are in pain and the government hasn’t been able to provide them with any relief. He put it even more bluntly. He spoke of the ‘system’ (the entire country — not just the one in Sindh) having collapsed. Not collapsing but collapsed. He said it wasn’t possible to deliver regardless of how hard the prime minister worked and how many long hours he put in. He referenced recent events in India , saying that if the ‘cockroaches’ (youth) got together, they would overthrow it all. But more intriguingly, he also made it clear that giving people a few thousand rupees or a laptop wasn’t enough. This was clearly a reference to the various schemes launched by the PML-N as well as the Benazir Income Support Programme, which is seen as the PPP’s baby. He proposed a solution by arguing the country needed more provinces or administrative units so that governance could be delivered at the doorstep. The next day, the DG ISPR reinforced this proposal . The interior minister’s indictment of the present government will not be forgotten easily. While his solution or proposal took no one by surprise, his criticism of the set-up did. After all, most of us are aware that there is much discussion behind closed doors on the need to revisit the NFC as well as the notion of devolution (which would assist the people as well as weaken the dynasty-controlled fiefdoms at the provincial level). However, Naqvi’s indictment of the present government will not be forgotten easily — for now, all those who had been waxing lyrical about the work done by Maryam Nawaz in Punjab or by Shehbaz Sharif at the centre will find it hard to argue that the party has delivered and won over the people. Interestingly, his remarks, which were a damning indictment of the current set-up, were initially met with silence. It took nearly a day before the reaction came from the PPP and PML-N whose public representatives are usually quick to hold media talks every day on any hint of criticism. But to contradict the interior minister, and one who is said to be very close to the highest in the establishment, is surely above the pay grade of those put in charge of information ministries. Still, the senior tiers were called to report for duty . In Sindh, the chief minister himself pooh-poohed the suggestion, while from the PML-N Rana Sanaullah was the first to fire back. Since then, others too have joined the fray, but most of the criticism focuses on Naqvi and not those who back him. There was also news of a family gathering at Jati Umrah in Lahore. Not much emerged from it other than some vloggers thundering about Nawaz Sharif having been woken up from his slumber — news that somehow didn’t get traction unlike Naqvi’s speech. Perhaps it is because the news is limited to a few who are relying on sources or because no one really believes the family is in a position to push back. The silence from the PPP heads is equally noticeable. In the meantime, the lower tiers might continue to thunder, though it is hard to believe Mohsin Naqvi will now respond to these allegations. But what now seems inevitable is another amendment to the Constitution, even if there is little clarity on what it will bring. New provinces and other wholesale changes (for it would mean reconfiguring the Senate)? Or simply a strong local government system with some federal areas? Or will it begin with easing the provisions for creating new provinces? Or a change in the NFC? Nothing is clear but the path ahead seems to lead to parliament. That Ahsan Bhoon was also present at the event where Naqvi spoke also indicates this. But while the powers that be have perhaps made their intentions clear, the silence from the parties means they are still to put together a strategy. Will they simply try to win over some concessions as they did during the previous two amendments? Will they drive a hard bargain? Or is the time and space for compromises over? The details are as above my pay grade as they are beyond the ability and position of Azma Bokhari or Atta Tarrar to respond to Naqvi. So as the hackneyed phrase goes, let’s wait and watch. However, it might just be safe to say that the amendment will not sail through without hiccups. It would mean a weakening of both the parties vis-à-vis the provincial governments, politically as well as in terms of patronage. For instance, the PPP will lose its political raison d’être; for Maryam Nawaz, the position of chief minister might lose its lustre, increasing the competition for the position in Islamabad. The initial instinct therefore will be to bargain and get something in return, if they decide not to push back. In other words, the hybrid system is now set for a new tug of war, which may leave some, if not all, of the stakeholders a little worse for wear. The writer is a journalist. Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

items.title: Swat bombing
items.description: IT is a bitter irony that terrorists struck a protest against violence in Swat on Sunday, causing at least 17 fatalities . Both policemen and civilians were martyred in the atrocity. Reports indicate that a suicide bomber blew himself up near a police station as the anti-terror protest was underway when officers tried to search him. Some media outlets have said the banned TTP has claimed responsibility for the bombing. This bloodbath should lead to thorough counterterrorism action, as the people of Swat — and indeed the rest of KP — deserve to live in an atmosphere free of terrorism and violence. Unfortunately, as pointed out in an exclusive report published in this paper, gaps in training have left LEAs in KP vulnerable to ‘double-tap’ or ‘two-stage’ attacks by terrorists. Moreover, the casualty numbers from July, and the first half of 2026, indicate that a fresh CT strategy is needed to bring down the number of fatalities, and effectively neutralise the threat of terrorism. The fact is that terrorists appear to be operating without fear of consequences, while LEAs are unable to stay ahead of them. A string of recent ‘two-stage’ attacks in KP illustrate this point. The terrorists’ modus operandi involves attacking security facilities, waiting for reinforcements to arrive, and then staging secondary attacks. A number of security personnel have been martyred in these attacks. Police officials say forces lack the training to counter these attacks, while experts also question how terrorists are able to maintain their supply lines. The gaps in training need to be filled so that security forces are able to defend themselves, gain the upper hand over violent elements, and, through better intelligence, break up their networks and thwart their attacks. At present, the terrorism figures, particularly in Balochistan and KP, do not paint a reassuring picture. According to the PICSS think tank , there were over 600 fatalities in July. While the vast majority was of terrorists, over 200 security men, civilians and peace committee members were martyred last month. Balochistan saw the highest levels of violence, while KP was not far behind. Overall, in the first six months of 2026, Pakistan has witnessed over 900 fatalities involving LEAs and civilians. This is far too high a toll, and the state needs to urgently refine its CT strategy to prevent further loss of precious lives. It is a matter of great concern that despite the martyrdom of so many policemen and soldiers, as well as civilians, the state is unable to vanquish the monster of terrorism. Hostile external forces may indeed be creating problems, but as security experts point out, we have failed to secure spaces within our borders where terrorists operate from. This continuous bloodbath must end so that people can live in peace. Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

items.title: España reprochará en Bruselas la reacción europea a la crisis de Ceuta
items.description: Tal vez sea una hipérbole calificar la migración como arma de destrucción masiva; probablemente los ceutíes no lo vieron de la misma manera el pasado fin de semana . Pero no es ningún exceso retórico argumentar que la política migratoria es a día de hoy el asunto más espinoso en la UE, con la ultraderecha cargando las tintas y la derecha, e incluso el centroizquierda escandinavo, sumándose a esa ola que tiene poco que ver con los valores que Europa dice defender. Una de las grandes excepciones es España, que está aplicando una regularización para cientos de miles de migrantes y políticas de apertura que explican, en parte, un avance del PIB muy por encima de las métricas europeas. Pero más de 60.000 personas han atravesado irregularmente las fronteras españolas —que son las de Europa— hace apenas unas horas, provocando una crisis de primera magnitud, y han reafirmado la soledad de España en esa agenda tan controvertida. Hasta 22 países capitaneados por una populista italiana, Giorgia Meloni , y la socialdemócrata danesa, Mette Frederiksen, cargaron con fuerza contra la España de Pedro Sánchez tras la avalancha ceutí con una mezcla extraña de hechos alternativos y amnesia de los valores europeos. La gélida reacción de la presidenta de la Comisión Europea, Ursula von der Leyen, dio pábulo a esos ataques, aunque este lunes –con la crisis en vías de solución— la alemana cambió el paso y adoptó un tono más conciliador. El Gobierno español, a pesar de los errores, resolvió el grueso del problema en 48 horas. Y este martes llega su turno: España, según las fuentes consultadas, reclamará en la cumbre de ministros del Interior solidaridad a los socios y afeará a los más duros lo que Pedro Sánchez ha calificado de “reacción egoísta, polarizadora e ilegal”, guiada por “prejuicios, fake news , ignorancia o interés político”. items.description: Paula Sánchez (Pontevedra, 47 años) se encontraba como todos los días frente a su monitor. Había pasado media vida gestionando cuentas, presupuestos y balances. Sabía leer números y anticipar amenazas. Aquella mañana de noviembre de 2025, cuando se topó con un anuncio de una vacante remota en LinkedIn no vio ningún riesgo. Para ella la oferta representaba un ingreso extra, una oportunidad compatible con su vida familiar y su trabajo como responsable administrativa. “Hola”, le escribió desde WhatsApp Sofía Koivu, una falsa reclutadora holandesa de ReSee, una boutique de lujo vintage afincada en París. Un mensaje llevó a otro y, en cuestión de horas, firmó un precontrato para ejercer el cargo de Marketing ranking associate con un salario base de 600 euros. “Solo tienes que ayudar a mejorar el posicionamiento de los productos”, le explicó la mujer. Era un chat más entre tantos, pero sin saberlo, ella estaba dando el primer paso hacia algo que no tenía nada que ver con un empleo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La asombrosa Venus de Alicante: una cabeza de 2.000 años asoma entre piedras, litronas y una bolsa del súper
items.description: Una excavadora abre una zanja cerca de la playa de la Almadraba, en Alicante, a 50 metros de un yacimiento arqueológico. Es un trabajo de canalización que forma parte del proyecto municipal de regeneración del arenal, situado entre la Albufereta y el Cabo de las Huertas. Al paso de la pala va apareciendo lo habitual, piedras, cantos rodados y hasta litronas de cerveza. Hasta que uno de los operarios da el alto. Entre todo el material de aluvión, surge una cabeza femenina de mármol blanco. Una superviviente de dos milenios de arrastre y aluvión, sin ningún contexto arqueológico, en buen estado, que acaba en una bolsa de Mercadona, protegida apenas por algo de papel burbuja. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los nuevos dueños de la Puerta del Sol son chinos y venden bisutería: “Tenemos menos miedo al riesgo”
items.description: En el entorno de la Puerta del Sol, menos de cien metros separan 12 tiendas de bisutería Miramira. Sus grandes carteles rosa y sus bajos precios son el principal reclamo y la compañía suma más de una decena de establecimientos en las calles que rodean el kilómetro cero, desde Arenal hasta Carmen y Preciados. Son resultado de un sigiloso movimiento: los empresarios chinos han pasado de regentar restaurantes y bazares diseminados por toda la ciudad a convertirse en los verdaderos dueños del codiciado centro de la capital. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Naufraga el polémico plan que pretendía crear en Canarias la primera granja de pulpos del mundo
items.description: Fin al polémico proyecto de implantar la primera granja de pulpos del mundo en el Puerto de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria. Nueva Pescanova informó la pasada semana a la Autoridad Portuaria de su solicitud de desistimiento del procedimiento de otorgamiento de concesión demanial —un permiso oficial que da el gobierno para usar un bien público de forma exclusiva, con un tiempo límite y pagando una tasa— para la instalación de una “Granja de Cultivos Marinos” en el puerto canario. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Pedro Pacheco: “Yo salí de la cárcel, pero la cárcel no ha salido de mí”
items.description: Pedro Pacheco fue alcalde de Jerez de la Frontera (Cádiz) durante 24 años –desde 1979 a 2003–, parlamentario andaluz y también europeo por el ya desaparecido Partido Andalucista, y se hizo famoso por acuñar una frase que tal vez determinó su futuro: “La justicia es un cachondeo”. Fue su reacción, en 1985, a la anulación, por parte de la Audiencia Territorial de Sevilla, de la orden de derribo del chalet que el cantante Bertín Osborne se había construido sin los preceptivos permisos urbanísticos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Ricos que no quieren ser ricos
items.description: “En Brasil hay más de 20 millones de madres solteras. Mujeres que, sin ayuda, tienen que luchar cada día para mantener a su familia. Yo soy una de ellas”. Así se dirigió Shakira a un público de dos millones de personas el pasado mayo en la playa de Copacabana . La frase llamó la atención por dos omisiones. La primera es conceptual: sus hijos tienen un padre, con quien —con el arreglo que sea— comparte la crianza, lo cual la excluye por definición de la categoría que reclama. La segunda, y más sorprendente aún, es material: un patrimonio estimado en 300 millones de dólares, que hace que luchar cada día sea más llevadero. En el calor del momento, a Shakira le pareció buena idea presentarse como una mujer normal tirando a apurada. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La Marcha Verde sobre Ceuta
items.description: En los estertores de la dictadura franquista, en noviembre de 1975, Hassan II promovió la Marcha verde sobre la colonia española del Sáhara español, lo que finalmente dio lugar a su ocupación hasta el día de hoy. La entrada masiva de personas, siendo la mayoría marroquíes, los últimos días de julio de 2026 en la ciudad autónoma de Ceuta supone también la instrumentalización de civiles con el objeto de alcanzar fines políticos. Esta instrumentalización no es nueva y, aunque no cuenta, como sí fue en 1975, con una convocatoria formal organizada, sí que presenta similitudes que hay que valorar, ya que, en ambos casos, el desplazamiento de población hacia un territorio bajo soberanía o administración española aparece vinculado a una estrategia clara de presión sobre Madrid y a la conversión de la frontera en un factor de coerción. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los alcaldes que se enfrentaron al peor incendio de la historia claman a Sánchez y Feijóo por un pacto: “Que se quiten la camiseta de partido ya”
items.description: Los cuatro se presentaron a la alcaldía de su pueblo para trabajar por sus vecinos y por las calles donde se curtieron desde niños. Los cuatro acaban de vivir —y padecer— uno de los episodios más tremendos al frente del bastón de mando de sus respectivos ayuntamientos, ninguno de más de 3.000 habitantes. Dos de las alcaldesas llegan de su última reunión en el Cecopi sobre el incendio más grave de la historia de España, el de Burgohondo en Ávila. Otro de los regidores baja del coche apenas unos minutos después de atender un nuevo conato en la sierra del Oeste, en Madrid. La cuarta pisa la tierra quemada con ansiedad, suplicando con la voz temblorosa que el fuego no vuelva a prender. Llenos de rabia, los cuatro regidores claman a las dos grandes fuerzas políticas, PSOE y PP, y demandan a sus máximos responsables, Pedro Sánchez y Alberto Núñez Feijóo, que dejen a un lado el abismo que les separa y negocien un pacto de Estado . “Que se quiten la camiseta de partido ya. O nos sentamos, o desapareceremos”, resume Vanessa Muñoz, edil socialista de 47 años al frente del Consistorio abulense de Casavieja, una de las localidades más asediadas por el infierno de las recientes llamas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Cataluña otea el final del túnel tras la aplicación de la amnistía a casi una veintena de encausados
items.description: El president Salvador Illa celebró el viernes, en el balance de curso justo antes de irse de vacaciones , que la ley de la amnistía ya se esté aplicando después de que el Tribunal de Justicia de la UE (TJUE) dictaminara que no contraviene el derecho comunitario. “He defendido desde el primer día que se aplique de forma ágil y eficiente. Y estoy contento de que algunas personas se hayan beneficiado”, sostuvo el jefe del Govern. El Ejecutivo catalán reivindica desde hace tiempo el cumplimiento de la norma para restituir la normalidad política tras la larga y dilatada década del procés . Con el goteo hasta ahora de 18 casos amnistiados, Cataluña, ahora si, otea el final del túnel, que culminará con la vuelta de Carles Puigdemont. Seguir leyendo El indulto parcial a Laura Borràs y los Presupuestos La cascada de personas amnistiadas ha coincidido en el tiempo con el indulto parcial del Gobierno a Laura Borràs, la expresidenta del Parlament, condenada a cuatro años de prisión y a 13 de inhabilitación por trocear contratos. El indulto ha comportado rebajarle la pena de cárcel a dos años para que no entre en prisión. El Ejecutivo se ampara en que ha tomado esa decisión acatando el consejo del Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Catalunya, que consideró excesiva su propia condena. Junts y la propia afectada insisten en que la pena, no amnistiable, siempre tuvo un claro componente de persecución política. Y el PP no ha tardado en considerar el perdón como un primer pago a cuenta de un eventual apoyo de Junts a los Presupuestos de 2027. Pedro Sánchez afirmó que el indulto parcial “nada tiene que ver con los presupuestos y con la negociación política”. La propia Miriam Nogueras dijo en la red que su rechazo a las cuentas es inamovible.

items.title: El verano al rojo vivo de Luís Montenegro al frente del Gobierno de Portugal
items.description: Parece el argumento de una novela negra, pero se queda en un escándalo que ha hecho tambalearse al Gobierno portugués. Un remolque con precursores químicos para fabricar cocaína que había sido decomisado en una operación antidroga en 2024 apareció entre los camiones de un constructor amigo de Luís Neves, ministro del Interior, a quien el empresario ha hecho algunas reformas en una propiedad… y a quien el ahora ministro, durante su etapa como director de la Policía Judicial (PJ), adjudicó varios contratos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Jordania, en el foco indeseado de la guerra de Oriente Próximo
items.description: El pasado 20 de julio, las sirenas antiaéreas sonaron por sorpresa en Amán, la capital de Jordania. Irán había lanzado cuatro misiles, que fueron interceptados o cayeron en zonas vacías, según el ejército. Es uno de los últimos ejemplos de cómo el país se ha convertido, a su pesar y junto con Kuwait, en el principal objetivo de los misiles y drones de Teherán en estas últimas semanas de montaña rusa ( mezcla de ataques, amenazas y diálogo ) a la que anda subido Oriente Próximo. La situación ha abierto un inhabitual debate sobre el precio que paga Jordania por su estrecha alianza de seguridad con EE UU y ha generado la paradoja de que sufre los ataques que, desde junio, no recibe Israel , que promovió e inició la guerra el pasado febrero, mano a mano con Washington, y desde donde salen aviones de EE UU para bombardear Irán. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El minuto y medio de fama de la España vaciada: el eclipse total ocultará el Camino de Santiago
items.description: El Camino de Santiago quedará sumido en la oscuridad en pleno día, a las 20.28 del 12 de agosto. A esa hora, una alargada sombra llegará a una velocidad hipersónica (más de 7.000 kilómetros por hora) y cubrirá al mismo tiempo prácticamente toda la ruta jacobea durante cerca de 1 minuto y 30 segundos. Solo el destino final —los últimos tramos, ya en Compostela— y las etapas iniciales de la peregrinación —hasta pasar Pamplona— seguirán viendo la luz del Sol, pues quedan fuera de la banda de totalidad del eclipse. Seguir leyendo ¿Y tú cómo vivirás el eclipse? En EL PAÍS, queremos saber cómo se preparan ustedes, nuestros lectores, para el fenómeno astronómico del 12 de agosto. Envíanos a participacion@elpais.es tu testimonio de cómo te preparas o cómo recibirá tu pueblo o ciudad el eclipse. Puedes incluir fotos si quieres. El próximo lunes, 10 de agosto, publicaremos algunas de las historias del eclipse de nuestros lectores.

items.title: El Satisfyer siete años después: “El robot rompió la brecha orgásmica, pero perjudicó a la masturbación más libre”
items.description: Fue el regalo estrella de las Navidades prepándemicas y ahí resiste, guardado en mi mesita de noche y en la de millones de españolas. Hace siete años, las mujeres de mi entorno se obsesionaron con él. Era “lo mejor” en sobremesas, en los pódcasts de las chicas listas, en grupos de WhatsApp y en la publicidad segmentada de Instagram. El Satisfyer, el succionador de clítoris, supuso un antes y después en el goce de las españolas. No solo por desterrar a la penetración en la ecuación del orgasmo femenino. Su facilidad de uso y el poco tiempo que requería para llegar al clímax fueron clave para convencer hasta las más reacias. Seguir leyendo

items.description: L’opération militaire ne provoquera pas un retrait rapide des troupes russes de la péninsule, mais elle rendra peut-être leur présence intenable sur la durée.

items.title: Helados y polos de peor a mejor: un ránking personal del Fantasmiko al Frigopie
items.description: Por fin llegó el verano (hace ya un rato, pero está bien comentarlo). Porque a quién no le van a gustar las máximas de 45º, los guiris llenando todas las playas y, por supuesto, el ritual de examinar el cartel de los helados del chiringuito de turno . Ese ritual de indecisión eterna en el que no sabes si arriesgar con algo nuevo o perpetuar la decisión que tomaste con seis años y que nunca, nunca moviste. Seguir leyendo

items.title: “Se aliaron con su peor enemigo”: cómo hace 2.400 años los persas fabricaron hielo en mitad del desierto
items.description: Aquí estamos otra vez, sudando bajo la dorsal atmosférica como insectos atrapados en una lupa cósmica, porque resulta que el cielo y el cambio climático —que se comporta como un dios menor. O mayor, ya veremos— han decidido que el verano de 2026 no será un verano sino una secuencia de hornos encadenados, una ola y luego otra y luego una tercera, cada una jurando que es la última y mintiendo, siempre mintiendo. El aeropuerto de Bilbao marcó 42,7 grados el 24 de junio, la cifra más alta jamás registrada allí en junio o julio, y eso que Bilbao es una ciudad que históricamente presume de su verde húmedo, de su orballo, de su no-ser-Sevilla. Y mientras tanto encendemos el aire acondicionado, un aparato que enfría la habitación calentando el planeta entero . Y al hacerlo, firmamos un pacto fáustico que nos vende frío a cambio de futuro, y nos sentimos modernos y a salvo, nos sentimos —pobres de nosotros— inteligentes. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Una callada revolución sentimental: por qué el 80% de los españoles ya cree en el amor sin sexo
items.description: Cada vez hay más parejas que se quieren profundamente y comparten piso, planes de futuro, hijos, vacaciones... El sexo no está fuera de la ecuación , pero es solo una variable más, y no la más importante. Al menos eso es lo que apuntan los datos del estudio del CIS publicado en enero bajo el título Percepción social del amor , que muestran hasta qué punto está cambiando la forma de entender el amor en España. Seguir leyendo

items.title: 144 children lost to diphtheria, measles since January in Karachi
items.description: • Deaths from vaccine-preventable diseases reported at four tertiary care city hospitals • Expert says most parents fail to ensure children receive recommended doses on time • EPI official claims cases declined this year KARACHI: At least 144 children have lost to measles and diphtheria — both vaccine-preventable infections — at four key tertiary care hospitals in the first seven months of this year, it emerged on Monday. Sources said that a total of 1,915 cases of measles with 125 mortalities have been reported at the four hospitals —Indus Hospital (IH), Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital and Research Centre (SIDH&RC), National Institute of Child Health (NICH) and Sindh Institute of Child Health and Neonatology (SICHN) — this year so far. Eighty-one cases of diphtheria were reported at SIDH&RC, eight at Indus Hospital (8) with 19 deaths. Detailed analysis of the data showed that at least 17 children have lost their lives to measles — a highly contagious viral infection — at IH with around 850 cases this year so far. In addition, a child died of diphtheria at the hospital, which has recorded at least eight of cases of the bacterial infection. At SID&RC, at least 54 children — 36 from measles and 18 from diphtheria — have died during the period between Jan 1 and July 26, 2026. The total number of measles and diphtheria cases reported at the facility was 575 and 81, respectively. While detailed data of the NICH was not available, sources at the province’s largest public-sector hospital for children shared that at least seven children have died of measles at the facility in recent weeks. “We get complicated cases after the patient has already been mismanaged at multiple health facilities. At that stage, measles has either turned into encephalitis [a dangerous swelling and inflammation of the brain] or pneumonia [the most common measles’ complication]. The former carries a significant risk of death and long-term disability,” a doctor at the NICH told Dawn on the condition of anonymity. Information gathered from SICHN showed that 484 cases of measles have been reported this year so far at the facility with 65 deaths. Role of healthcare providers Explaining why a significant number of children couldn’t get protection against diseases that could easily be prevented through vaccines available free of cost under the Expanded Programme for Immunisation (EPI), Dr Khalid Shafi of the Pakistan Paediatric Association said that the tragedy in Pakistan was that the coverage rate of vaccine doses given at birth was 90 per cent but this number declined sharply as the child grows, requiring subsequent doses of vaccines. “Unfortunately, parents get negligent and the child either gets no or partial protection against several diseases including measles, typhoid and polio,” he said, adding that around 20 to 25 per cent of the child population in the country couldn’t get timely vaccination. He pointed out that the first shot of measles under the EPI programme was given at nine months and the second (the last) one at 15 months. “If 95 per cent of our children get the two shots at the right time, we can easily control this disease as the vaccine provides herd immunity to the rest of the population. Most children in our country, however, either fail to receive any dose or get only partial protection through one dose.” To address this challenge, he said countrywide vaccination drives were launched every four years. Last year, a national level drive was launched for children aged six months to five years, who were given an additional dose of MR (measles and rubella) vaccine. “Along with the government efforts, our healthcare providers have a crucial role to help tackle the vaccination coverage gap. When an ailing child reports to them, they must ask about his or her vaccination history/status and provide proper counselling to parents, if they find any vaccine doses missing. “Having said that, parents have the prime responsibility to protect their child and they must play their part with diligence. Though there are cases with children falling sick despite getting the vaccine shots, their numbers are few and the disease intensity in such cases is mild.” EPI’s response In his response, EPI Project Director Dr Raj Kumar said cases of measles and diphtheria had declined this year in the province, especially measles which saw a 35 per cent drop. According to him, 148 cases of diphtheria with 14 deaths were reported in the province in the first seven months of 2025, while this year so far 10 deaths have been reported with 46 confirmed cases. “Last year, we had 4,626 cases of measles in the first seven months with 57 deaths in the province. This year so far, we have 3,025 cases with 59 deaths,” he said. Highlighting challenges, he said that pockets of unvaccinated children and parental negligence were primary drivers of increase in cases. “Along with that, there are myths surrounding me­­asles and parents prefer traditional remedies, keep their child at home, resulting in disease complications,” he explained, adding that the government had run vaccination campaigns to cover missed children and planning to continue this process and that an additional 970 vaccinators had been recruited to address HR shortages. The government had surveillance units and collected data from hospitals, he said. Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

items.title: A Family Tragedy in the Age of Trump
items.description: O nce upon a time, it was practically de minimis for either political party to disavow a candidate facing allegations of domestic violence. But now is not that time. Which might help to explain why as the divorce of young MAGA royalty— Ohio Representative Max Miller and Emily Moreno, daughter of Ohio Senator Bernie Moreno—has morphed from a deeply personal family tragedy into a highly public political spectacle, Republicans have been reluctant to say that an alleged domestic abuser (especially one facing allegations from two women) is probably a poor choice to represent their party this November. I am referring, of course, to Miller, who Emily Moreno has accused of scalding her with hot water, holding a gun to her head, and throwing her against a wall—all allegations he has denied. (She also suggested that because of his history of violence against her, she couldn’t rule out that he had fractured their daughter’s collarbone, which he also denies.) But this is now a party whose leader has been accused of sexual misconduct by more than two dozen women; a party whose president was found liable in a civil trial for sexually abusing and defaming writer E. Jean Carroll; a party whose chief once palled around with Jeffrey Epstein , the notorious convicted sex offender. And so perhaps only in President Trump’s Republican Party does believing all women—or even some women, some of the time—become politically fraught. [ Read: The grim aftermath of the E. Jean Carroll verdict ] Bernie Moreno declared yesterday that Miller should not serve in the House of Representatives, writing on X that the past two years have been “pure hell” for his family. “Max Miller needs serious psychological help,” Moreno wrote. “He is a danger to my daughter, and I hold my breath every minute he has custody of my granddaughter.” He concluded by saying that he owed it to his wife, “to Emily, and to my granddaughter to speak the truth now.” Moreno’s statement came after Miller appeared on a roughly 20-minute live stream that morning, in which he refused to drop out of his House race and explained that he strived to comport himself with “dignity” for the sake of his daughter—all while proceeding to publicly impugn his daughter’s mother. Initially, Moreno found himself on a tiny island of Republicans who believe that an alleged domestic abuser is not fit to serve in Congress. When Trump was asked on Air Force One yesterday if he thought Miller should resign, he said he would “look at it,” but noted, “so far it’s accusations.” He repeated that stance in the Oval Office this afternoon, calling Miller “a good person” and suggesting that this is a situation that needs to be resolved within the family, not within the party. A representative for Miller declined to comment. But by this evening, as the Senate returned and reporters pressed lawmakers on Miller’s fate, a growing number of Republicans conceded that maybe he wasn’t the best candidate, after all. Trump also reportedly called Miller today to express concerns about his candidacy, according to Axios . But a person familiar with Trump’s concerns told me that even if the president pushed Miller to bow out, they weren’t certain the young House member would heed the president’s advice. C laims of misbehavior and anger issues have dogged Miller since at least high school, and Emily Moreno is not the first woman to accuse him of being violent. When Miller first ran for office in 2021, former White House communications director Stephanie Grisham said that when she dated him during Trump’s first term, their relationship had turned physically abusive. (Grisham wrote in a Washington Post op-ed in October 2021 that she told both President Trump and First Lady Melania Trump, for whom she also worked, about the abuse, and they did nothing.) Miller denied the accusations and sued Grisham for defamation, before dropping the lawsuit as part of a confidential settlement. That same year, a Politico profile of Miller recounted several brushes he had with authorities when he was younger, including charges of assault, disorderly conduct, and resisting arrest as a high school senior. The story also detailed how Miller allegedly pushed a girl out of his room after she resisted his advances, and she fell down some stairs, an incident sourced to three people who said they were present at the time and more who said they heard about the incident in the aftermath. At the time, Miller told Politico through a lawyer that he “categorically denies” the event. A description in that profile from someone who knew Miller during his earlier years—and described him as someone who “could be very scary”—has stayed with me: “I can, like, see the red face.” [ From the June issue: The men who want women to be quiet ] In mid-July, a Mother Jones piece unearthed new allegations against Miller, based on more than 2,000 pages of court filings and police reports that writer Abby Vesoulis obtained through public records requests that contain “allegations of drug use by Miller, misogyny and verbal abuse, and violent behavior against multiple women,” she writes. A report about a collarbone injury his daughter suffered, for instance, includes Emily Moreno telling investigators that her daughter told her, “Daddy’s house is scary.” (Miller’s spokesperson did not directly address all of the magazine’s questions, but pointed to previous statements Miller and his representatives have made to other news organizations, denying he has ever been violent toward women.) Then, a New York Times article last week brought more attention to the allegations, raising uncomfortable questions for the Republican Party about why its members seem so reluctant to suggest that Miller step aside. For a time, this included Moreno himself. I am not unsympathetic to Bernie Moreno. I am the stepmom in a blended family, and I understand a key tenet of Divorce 101, especially when there are kids, is to never speak ill of anyone involved. Moreno seemed to be trying to abide by that ideal. In a recorded conversation between Miller and Emily Moreno—made public yesterday when Miller released a collection of documents, videos and audio clips he says will help exonerate him—she described being upset Miller had lashed out at her father, noting, “My dad, despite what you may think, has never said negative things about you to me, even to this day, through this process.” She added that when she told her dad that other people have, post-divorce, discouraged her from being in regular contact with Miller, her dad disagreed and reminded her that Miller is still the father of her daughter. Two people close to the family told me Moreno’s initial silence was at his daughter’s request: Emily Moreno does not want her own daughter to one day read about her grandfather attacking her dad. One of these people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because of the fraught nature of the dispute, added that because of the ongoing litigation, Moreno was reluctant to say anything publicly that Miller’s lawyers would almost certainly try to use against his family, and he also feared that Miller could take out any anger toward the senator on his daughter and granddaughter. A second person close to Emily Moreno offered a similar assessment. A third person familiar told me the entire Moreno family had hoped to prevent the divorce from becoming a vicious spectacle, and that while the senator had wanted to speak out for months, he did not out of respect for his daughter and granddaughter, but has always supported her privately—including paying her legal fees, which now run in the hundreds of thousands. Nonetheless, Miller was quick to attack Moreno’s seemingly belated response, writing yesterday on X: “If my daughter said the same thing to me, I personally wouldn’t wait two years before holding him accountable. You know this isn’t true and the only reason you are speaking out now is to hide from your own media circus. This is all political.” And Moreno—not unlike many Republicans who at first remained silent on the Miller scandal, pleading they were not equipped to weigh in on mere allegations—has had no problem using allegations to go after Democratic opponents in the past. In a June Senate hearing, the senator alluded to the ongoing scandals involving then-Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner in a quest to “just do a little vetting here this morning.” He asked the assembled nominees before him: “Do any of you have a Nazi tattoo?” and “Have any of you ever said that women deserve to be raped and should take accountability for being intoxicated?” In an April hearing, Moreno took aim at Democrat Eric Swalwell, who had just resigned from Congress and ended his bid for California governor amid his own allegations of sexual misconduct. “What’s interesting to me is you look at the depraved individuals that serve in this body, people like Eric Swalwell —I don’t know that I’d want to be categorized the same way,” Moreno said. Which is why, on Friday, when NOTUS asked Moreno if Republicans should replace Miller on the ticket—the deadline to do so is Wednesday—because of the accusations of domestic violence, I was surprised by the senator’s tepid reply: “I don’t know.” [ Read: A police report about a House candidate surprised the White House ] Profile in courage this was not, as many Democrats (and former Republicans) pointed out online. “Be the kind of father who doesn’t tolerate a man who abused his daughter,” Sarah Longwell, the anti-MAGA political strategist and founder of The Bulwark , wrote on X. And from former Republican congressman Adam Kinzinger: “Imagine if your dad picked his job over you. @berniemoreno is a despicable man.” To his critics, the NOTUS story was just another example of cowardice by Moreno and his party. To those who know him well, the ensuing response was yet another reminder that anything can be used for political gain, even a family’s anguish. Tonight, when reporters pressed Moreno about why it took him some time to issue a statement about Miller, his long-simmering anger seeped out. “I hope you never have to go through a situation like this, and you wouldn’t ask that kind of fucking question,” he said. M iller and Emily Moreno’s relationship started like a MAGA romance novel: A marriage of two young MAGA scions—both from politically powerful and wealthy Ohio families—held at the president’s gilded Bedminster Club in August 2022 and attended by Trump himself. A father-in-law and son-in-law with big political ambitions, sharing the same midwestern state. But it did not end that way. Divorce filings came almost exactly two years later, in August 2024, along with mutual restraining orders issued the same day, and nasty accusations soon followed. In his live stream yesterday, Miller denied that he was violent with his ex-wife, pointing to messages between them several days after an alleged incident, in which she offered to cook him dinner. (To Miller, this exchange is exonerating; to many people familiar with domestic abuse, this exchange is also typical of how victims sometimes try to salvage their relationships or protect themselves and their kids.) Miller also, claiming to speak from “great sadness, and not anger,” cast his ex-wife as mentally ill, saying he did not mention this “to embarrass her, or to attack her”—despite spending the majority of his address doing just that. The situation, he said, has been painful for everyone involved, “especially our daughter, who we both need to think about more so than ever, and I feel as if I am the only one who does.” Then, for a man interested in protecting his daughter, and convincing the public he’s not the controlling abuser his ex-wife claims, he added a confusing coda: “She is a beautiful, innocent child, and she didn’t ask for any of the media scrutinization of her family, and she will eventually see all of these reports one day, as she will continue to bear my last name—Miller.” I began digging into the documents Miller released that he said would refute his ex-wife’s claims. The collection includes a series of text messages between the two parents, filled with the quotidian challenges of life with a toddler, all further exacerbated by divorce—screen time concerns, balancing work and childcare, birthday party drop-offs. And then there was this: Emily Moreno told Miller in February that their daughter was having another anxiety attack, similar to one she’d had previously. Miller responded: “Ugh, hold her tight and snuggle with her. I hate this for her. The only remedy I know is just to hold her tight and snuggle.” The two go back and forth a few more times—with Emily Moreno expressing concern that their daughter told her, “Daddy kill you” and Miller arguing “there is no way she is saying that”—before Moreno offers another update the following morning. “She woke up once in middle of night for cuddles but overall much better.” Marie-Rose Sheinerman contributed to this report.

items.title: Marché des capitaux: plus de 55,04 MMDH de levées à fin juin 2026

Ces levées comprennent principalement les émissions de titres de créances négociables (TCN) avec 39,29 MMDH et les émissions obligataires totalisant 14,35 MMDH, précise l'AMMC dans ses indicateurs mensuels du marché des capitaux du mois de juin. S'y ajoutent les émissions de titres de capital s'élevant à 1,4 MMDH, fait savoir la même source. Concernant l'encours des opérations de prêt emprunt de titres, il a atteint 47,9 MMDH à fin juin 2026, en baisse de 9% depuis le début de l'année, mais en hausse de 31% en glissement annuel. Pour le seul mois de juin 2026, les levées de capitaux ont été de 13,36 MMDH, dont 6,49 MMDH provenant des émissions de TCN, 6,05 MMDH des émissions obligataires et 822 millions de dirhams des émissions de titres de capital. items.title: Heavy rain warning raises flood risk in low-lying areas
items.description: • Medium to high flows expected in nullahs linked to Jhelum, Chenab and Ravi • Authorities on high alert as NDMA reviews flood preparedness LAHORE: While rising river flows have pushed Tarbela Dam near its maximum capacity, the Met Office has warned of urban flooding and inundation in low-lying areas of several cities as heavy monsoon rains are expected on Tuesday (today). According to the Flood Forecasting Divi­sion (FFD) of the Pakistan Meteorological De­­­­partment, heavy rainfall may trigger wat­er accumulation in low-lying areas of Islam­abad, Rawalpindi, Lahore, Sheikhupura, Kasur, Faisalabad, Multan, Sahiwal, Okara, Bahawalnagar, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Sialkot, the Potohar region, Peshawar and Nowshera. The division also warned of flash flooding in hill torrents and local streams across Kashmir, Murree, Galiyat, northeastern Punjab, Islamabad, the Potohar region, some areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Dera Ghazi Khan. Medium to high flows are expected in nullahs linked to the Jhelum, Chenab and Ravi rivers, while flash floods are also likely in the hill torrents of Dera Ghazi Khan, streams in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the Kabul River and its tributaries, and parts of northern Balochistan. Landslides are also feared in the mountainous districts of upper Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, including Dir, Swat, Kohistan, Buner, Battagram, Mansehra, Shangla and Abbottabad, as well as Murree, Galiyat and the hilly areas of Azad Kashmir. The FFD said the Indus River at Kalabagh, Guddu and Sukkur, and the Ravi at Balloki, are currently flowing at low flood level. It urged all relevant authorities to remain on alert and take precautionary measures to deal with possible rain-related emergencies. According to the Water and Power Development Authority’s (Wapda) daily water report, the Indus at Tarbela recorded inflows of 250,700 cusecs and outflows of 191,900 cusecs on Monday. The Kabul River at Nowshera recorded both inflows and outflows of 43,700 cusecs, while the Jhelum at Mangla registered inflows of 44,700 cusecs and outflows of 7,000 cusecs. The Chenab at Marala recorded inflows of 85,900 cusecs and outflows of 69,900 cusecs. The report showed that Tarbela Dam’s water level had risen to 1,543 feet, only seven feet below its maximum conservation level of 1,550 feet, with live storage reaching 5.178 million acre-feet (MAF). Mangla Dam’s water level stood at 1,199.35 feet, around 42 feet below its maximum conservation level of 1,242 feet, with live storage of 4.193 MAF. Chashma Reservoir is also nearing full capacity, with its water level recorded at 648.50 feet against a maximum conservation level of 649 feet. Monsoon, flood preparedness Meanwhile, National Disaster Manage­me­­nt Authority (NDMA) Chairman retired Lt Gen Inam Haider Malik visited the Punjab Disaster Management Authority (PDMA) headquarters to review monsoon and flood preparedness across the province. He was received by Punjab Minister Kha­waja Salman Rafique and PDMA Director General Saif Anwar Jappa. The NDMA chairman visited the Provincial Emergency Control Centre, where officials briefed him on preparedness measures, while climate change, resource management and capacity building also came under discussion. Mr Rafique said all departments, including health, rescue and livestock, were fully mobilised to respond to any flood emergency. He said Rescue 1122 had been equipped with modern equipment worth billions of rupees, while new warehouses were being established across Punjab to improve emergency response. The NDMA chairman said the authority was maintaining close coordination with all provinces and that PDMA, Rescue 1122 and other institutions were responding effectively to the evolving monsoon situation. The PDMA director general said officials were continuously monitoring river flows and the monsoon situation across the province. He said underground water storage tanks were being constructed to reduce urban flooding, while Wasa had been equipped with modern machinery and its operations expanded to 41 cities. During the visit, the NDMA chairman presented commemorative shields to Mr Rafique and Mr Jappa. Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

items.title: PCB moves IHC against orders to disclose players’ financial details
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Pak­istan Cricket Board (PCB) has approached the Islam­abad High Court (IHC), challenging two separate orders of the Pakistan Information Commission (PIC) directing the board to disclose extensive financial, contractual and operational information relating to national cricketers, selection committee members and other PCB officials under the Right of Access to Information Act, 2017. The petitions, filed through Advocate Kashif Ali Malik, are fixed for hearing before IHC Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar. The first petition challenges the PIC’s order of July 9, requiring the PCB to disclose its annual budgets for the financial years 2023 to 2025, along with a detailed breakdown of expenditure; policies governing the confidentiality and disclosure of such information; details of players and officials who travelled for this year’s T20 World Cup; and details of the board’s audit mechanisms and reports. The second petition relates to information concerning Pakistan’s ODI series against South Africa held at Iqbal Stadium, Faisalabad, in November 2025. Through its order, the PIC directed the PCB to provide a breakdown of revenue, expenditure and details of steps taken or proposed to upgrade Iqbal Stadium for hosting PSL Season 12. Board claims disclosure orders threaten commercial interests, privacy rights of players Since taking office in 2024, PCB Chairman Mohsin Naqvi has stopped publishing the board’s financial statements on the PCB website. These statements had previously detailed expenditure across all departments, including the chairman’s office. The PCB has contended that it operates in a highly competitive international sporting environment and, unlike government departments funded through the public exchequer, receives no funding from the federal government or the Consoli­dated Fund. Instead, it says its revenues are generated primarily through commercial activities, including broa­dcasting rights, sponsorship agreements, media rights, gate receipts, licensing arrangements, international cricket events and distributions from the Inte­rnational Cricket Council. In its petitions, the PCB argues that the impugned orders wrongly assume that all information sought is subject to disclosure under Section 5 of the Right of Access to Information Act, 2017, while ignoring the Act’s express exemptions protecting personal privacy, confidential contractual arrangements, commercially sensitive information and third-party interests under Section 16. It contends that the information sought extends beyond institutional expenditure to confidential contractual and personal financial information of identifiable individuals, without recognising the distinction between institutional transparency and private financial affairs. The PCB submitted that disclosure of confidential remuneration structures and contractual terms would prejudice its commercial interests and contractual negotiations. The board also sought interim relief, arguing that once confidential contractual and personal financial information entered the public domain, the resulting prejudice to its commercial interests, contractual relationships and the privacy rights of third parties would be irreversible. Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

items.title: Pakistan gets a pass on new US visa bond rule
items.description: • Washington makes visa bond programme permanent; Bangladesh, Nepal among 50 countries covered, India also excluded • Visitors from listed nations face refundable deposits of up to $20,000 WASHINGTON: Pakistan is not among the 50 countries whose citizens may now be required to deposit up to $20,000 as a financial guarantee before obtaining a US visitor visa under a new programme that took effect on Aug 1. The list published in the US Federal Register does not include Pakistan. Among South Asian countries, Bangladesh and Nepal are covered by the programme, while India is not. Afghanistan and Iran are not included because the United States does not maintain normal diplomatic relations with either country. The State Department said the decision followed a review of the 2025 pilot programme, which it said significantly reduced visa overstays among travellers from participating countries and improved compliance with US immigration rules. Officials said those findings prompted Washington to make the programme permanent. According to the department, there were 45,488 overstays from these 50 countries in 2024. In the first 10 months of the pilot, the number of overstays was fewer than 50. The visa bond requirement has also resulted in a decrease in visa issuance, as some applicants appear to self-select by not paying a bond. Diplomatic sources also confirmed to Dawn that “Pakistan is not on the list of countries covered by the programme”. The programme applies to applicants for B-1 business and B-2 tourist visas from countries covered by the scheme. Under the new rules, US consular officers may require selected applicants to post a refundable bond of between $10,000 and $20,000 before issuing a visa. The regulations make permanent a visa bond pilot launched in 2025 after the US State Department concluded that it had helped reduce visa overstays. The new rules also increase the maximum bond from $15,000 to $20,000 and eliminate the previous $5,000 minimum bond available during the pilot programme. The 50 countries covered by the programme include 30 African nations as well as countries in Asia, the Caribbean and the Pacific. The bond will be refunded if the visitor complies with all visa conditions and leaves the United States before the authorised period of stay expires. Applicants who overstay or otherwise violate the terms of their visas risk forfeiting the deposit. The bond requirement does not apply automatically to all applicants from the countries covered by the programme. Instead, US consular officers will determine on a case-by-case basis whether a bond is warranted before issuing a visa. Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

items.title: Govt executes agreements with pension fund managers
items.description: • 16 companies to establish separate pension funds, ensure death and disability risk cover for employees • Centre to establish non-banking finance company to assist in implementation, monitoring of pension scheme ISLAMABAD: The government has executed agreements with 16 pension fund managers to formally operationalise the Defined Contribution Pension Fund Scheme (DCPFS) launched a year ago for public sector employees as part of major pension reforms aimed at containing the snowballing pension burden on the budget. In an announcement, the Ministry of Finance said it had executed agreements with 16 eligible pension fund managers, most of them banks and insurance companies. Around 10 of these eligible fund managers are owned or led by major commercial banks in the country. They include ABL Asset Management Company, Al Habib Asset Management, Al Meezan Investment, Faysal Asset Management, JS Investments, MCB Investment, Alfalah Asset Management, HBL Asset Management, UBL Fund Managers and NBP Fund Management, The pension fund managers led by or owned by insurance companies include EFU Life Assurance and Pak-Qatar Family Takaful. The remaining funds — Atlas Asset Man­agement, Lucky Invest­ments, National Investments and AWT Investments are owned by various business groups. Under the agreements and rules, these fund managers would set up, operate and manage conventional or Shariah-compliant funds for state employees under the federal government-defined contributory pension fund scheme in accordance with the Voluntary Pension System Rules 2005. Only these eligible pension fund managers shall be authorised to launch and manage employer pension funds for which the government will ensure annual budgetary allocation for the employer’s contribution. The agreements entail standard terms and conditions for providing systems support and electronic transfer of contributions to the pension fund’s designated bank accounts and further allocation of units to the relevant sub-funds in each employee’s pension account as per the allocation policy. The agreements also envisage a mandatory insurance plan, providing death and disability risk cover to the employees, to be arranged by these fund managers. The eligible pension fund managers will establish separate pension funds, while the government is responsible for the creation of a Non-Banking Finance Company (NBFC) to assist in implementation and monitoring of the pension fund scheme. Till such time the NBFC is established and fully operationalised, the government itself, through the finance ministry, will perform the NBFC role and establish an online portal to facilitate opening of pension accounts of employees, obtain information and data from eligible pension fund managers or otherwise communicate with the fund managers. Under the rules, employees will not withdraw any amount from the pension account before retirement is notified. Even upon reaching retirement age, the employee shall not withdraw more than 25pc of the accumulated balance in the pension account, and shall invest the remaining amount in the manner prescribed in the Voluntary Pension System Rules, 2005, for a period of at least twenty years or till his death, whichever is earlier. However, the rules allow employees to transfer pension account balance from one eligible pension fund manager to another. The government had announced pension reforms in 2024 to introduce a contributory pension fund for all government employees, including civil government and armed forces personnel. In a formal announcement in the National Assembly, the government said the contributory pension scheme would apply to all civil employees of the federal government, including civilian employees paid from defence estimates appointed on a regular basis on or after July 1, 2024. A September 2024 notification stated that the scheme would also apply to armed forces personnel appointed on or after July 1, 2025. While the civilian side of the scheme has been implemented and the government has already set aside about Rs25bn for the scheme as its initial share, the contributory pension scheme for armed forces was deferred for a year to 2026 due to concerns over their peculiar nature of duties requiring detailed review, according to earlier statements by the finance minister and secretary. Officials said the contributory pension scheme for armed forces personnel, which had been postponed two years ago, had been further delayed owing to internal departmental consultations and challenging security conditions, hindering any move that could be seen demoralising personnel. The finance ministry notified in October 2025 that federal employees would contribute 10pc of their pensionable pay to qualify for a 12pc contribution from the public exchequer under the newly formalised contributory pension fund scheme. The total contribution rate will thus be 22pc, replacing the traditional pension system for new entrants. The October notification and pension rules superseded an earlier order of August 2024, which had set the government’s contribution at 20pc. On Aug 20, 2024, the ministry initially announced the introduction of the contributory pension scheme for new entrants to the civil government and armed forces. At that time, employees were to contribute 10pc of their basic pay, while the government was to contribute 20pc. The contributory pension scheme was introduced on the advice of international lenders, notably the World Bank, to contain the rising pension liabilities, which the government had itself described as a growing fiscal risk. It does not apply to existing employees but aims to slow future growth in pension liabilities. Federal pension expenditure is estimated at Rs1.170tr for FY2026-27, including about Rs860bn for military pensions and about Rs300bn for civil employees. The pension budget had increased from Rs1.055tr in 2025-26. Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

items.title: Cotton production jumps 32 per cent
items.description: Textile mills have become reliant on imports amid falling cotton output.—PPI/file LAHORE: Phutti (seed-cotton) arrivals at ginning factories rose by more than 32 per cent year-on-year by July 31, driven by a sharp increase in Sindh despite a slight decline in Punjab, according to the figures released by the Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association (PCGA) on Monday. The PCGA fortnightly report revealed that phutti arrivals reached 785,822 bales by July 31, up 32.33pc from 593,821 bales received during the corresponding period last year. It showed that Punjab’s arrivals stood at 298,150 bales, down 1.1 per cent from a year earlier, while Sindh recorded 487,672 bales, marking a record 66.82pc increase despite recent monsoon rains. Balochistan also posted a 52.67pc rise in arrivals to 22,900 bales. Cotton Ginners Forum Chairman Ihsanul Haq pointed out a significant discrepancy between the PCGA figures and the Punjab government’s Crop Reporting Service (CRS). While the PCGA data showed phutti arrivals in Punjab at around 298,000 bales, the CRS claimed production of about 435,000 bales by July 30, roughly 32pc higher than the PCGA estimate. He said the difference warranted clarification from the relevant authorities. Sindh’s record 67pc surge by July 31 offsets Punjab decline despite rains He said the CRS figures also reflected an alarming collapse in cotton cultivation across Bahawalpur Division, where only around 17,000 bales were produced despite the region once being Pakistan’s leading cotton-growing belt. According to him, the rapid expansion of sugarcane cultivation, driven by the concentration of sugar mills in the region, has transformed the traditional cotton zone into a sugarcane belt, undermining domestic cotton production. Mr Haq warned that shrinking cotton acreage, due to increasing sugarcane sowing, was forcing the country to rely increasingly on imports of both cotton and edible oil. He urged the federal and provincial governments to restore cotton cultivation by restricting sugarcane farming in designated cotton-growing areas. Pakistan imported a record 3.482 million tonnes of edible oil worth $3.785 billion in 2025-26, compared with 3.214m tonnes valued at $3.40bn a year earlier. The PCGA report showed that textile mills purchased 704,000 bales, while exporters bought 3,400 bales, leaving 78,044 bales unsold at ginning factories. A total of 231 ginning factories were operational across the country, including 108 in Punjab and 123 in Sindh, although some units had either become partially operational or suspended operations due to financial and commercial constraints. Sanghar district alone accounted for 398,000 bales, representing 82pc of Sindh’s production and 51pc of the national total, largely because cotton sown in the province’s coastal areas during February and March had reached the market earlier than crops in other regions. Commenting on the latest arrivals, Sajid Mahmood, head of the Transfer of Technology Department at the Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI), Multan, said the early-season figures suggested a stronger start than last year, particularly in Sindh where timely sowing, harvesting and improved crop management had supported higher arrivals. However, he cautioned that August and September would provide a more reliable indication of the overall crop. He also warned that prolonged humidity and rainfall could increase the incidence of whitefly, pink bollworm and crop diseases, affecting lint quality and yields. He advised growers to ensure proper drainage, closely monitor pest populations and adopt plant protection measures in consultation with agricultural extension officials. Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

items.title: Pakistan to host Iranian officials as Trump’s patience wears thin
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakis­tan on Monday invited Iran’s parliament speaker and foreign minister for urgent consultations on regional developments, as Tehran described Islamabad as its primary mediator with the US. National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq invited Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran’s chief negotiator with Washington and speaker of parliament. Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, meanwhile, invited his Iranian counterpart, Seyyed Abbas Araghchi. The invitations were delivered in Tehran late Monday night after Dar spoke with Araghchi. “They exchanged views on regional and international developments, including the deteriorating situation in Occupied East Jerusalem,” the Foreign Office said in a statement. It remained unclear when Ghalibaf and Araghchi would travel to Pakistan. A diplomatic source said both men had been asked to come as soon as possible for discussions on regional and international developments. Araghchi was in Iraq on Monday for Arbaeen , which is being observed on Tuesday. The invitations came roughly 36 hours after US President Donald Trump announced he had canceled imminent strikes against Iran. Trump said allies had urged him to hold off because a deal appeared imminent. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke with Trump and persuaded him to call off the planned military action. Trump had also named UAE and Qatar as among the countries that had asked him to cancel the planned strikes. Iran has been holding talks with Oman about the future of the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian authorities say they are close to an agreement but have not indicated whether the waterway would reopen or remain closed. Pakistan has been relatively quiet on the mediation front compared with earlier efforts that produced the Islamabad MoU. It has, however, remained engaged through back channels with Iran and, together with Qatar, proposed a ceasefire plan during a nearly 13-day period of escalation. Iran’s foreign ministry on Monday insisted that Pakistan is the main mediator with US. Spokesman Esmail Baqaei said: “The mediator in the discussions related to Iran and the US is Pakistan, and Qatar also helps in cases where necessary. To say that we have added a new mediator to the existing mediators is not, in the strict sense of the word, the case.” Meanwhile, President Donald Trump accused Iran’s leadership of being “unbelievably duplicitous” after Tehran denied that any negotiations were underway with the US. The exchange renewed threats from Trump, who warned Iran faced “decapitation” and said he would keep up military pressure until there was a “deal, or total surrender”. “I think we’re going to maybe get something, but I want to give them every last chance before decapitation,” Trump said, reiterating his threat to launch a major attack on Iran. The war of words follows a familiar pattern in the five-month conflict between Washington and Tehran. The president, who on Sunday said renewed talks would begin “tomorrow afternoon” without naming a venue or participants, added that the US Navy maintains complete control over the Strait of Hormuz. “Nothing gets through to Iran, unless we want it to, and nothing will get through, unless a deal, or total surrender, is accomplished,” he said. Trump had told reporters aboard Air Force One that Iran, along with Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar, had asked him to hold off on what he claimed would have been “the biggest attack since World War II”. “Would I rather make a deal? I’m not looking to kill people,” Trump said on Sunday. He described ongoing discussions as a “last chance for them to sign a good document”. With input from Agencies Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

items.title: Senate body slams linking members to seizure of smuggled cigarettes
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The subcommittee of the Senate Standing Committee on Interior and Narcotics Control on Monday strongly condemned what it called a “malicious media campaign” targeting its members following the seizure of 11 trucks allegedly loaded with smuggled cigarettes on the motorway. The meeting, convened by Senator Saifullah Abro at Parliament House, was mandated to scrutinise border security mechanisms, smuggling networks, anti-narcotics controls, and tax evasion, including an estimated $1 billion attributed to the tobacco sector. The convener of the committee noted that after the July 20 meeting discussed the truck seizure, an official press release and handout were circulated the next day on TV channels targeting the committee chairman and members. The committee directed the Member of FBR to personally review the handout issued by his media wing and identify officials responsible. The FIA has also been tasked with conducting a “completely impartial, full-scale inquiry” into TV channels running target­­ed smear campaigns and submit a report. On the seizure of 11 trucks laden with smuggled cigarettes, the committee questioned jurisdiction, stating that Motorway operations fall under the Inland Revenue and not Customs. It raised alarm over “contradictory valuation figures amounting to Rs220 million and ordered owners of the transport and steel company concerned to submit a full report by Monday evening. It also questioned the legal basis of the FIR registered by Customs, noting that 11 truck drivers were arrested and produced in the court after a six-day delay. The inspector who drafted the FIR has been summoned. The Deputy Collector of Customs was directed to explain why political figures present at the site were omitted from the official reporting. The IG of Motorway Police clarified that an MoU exists with Customs only for “operational assistance in stopping suspicious vehicles”. The committee expressed shock that manual consumption certificates are still being issued despite digital policy, and questioned whether physical verification visits are conducted before issuance. It termed details provided on Rs1,120 billion of tax-exempted imports “completely unsatisfactory and incomplete” and ordered a comprehensive breakdown of local market sales against 2025-26 Quota Registration details. The subcommittee reaffirmed its commitment to unearth malpractices across Customs posts, dry ports, and revenue bodies, and directed the FIA to finalise inquiries. Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

Hervé Renard de retour sur le banc des Eléphants?
items.description: Libre depuis la fin de son passage à la tête de la sélection tunisienne en Coupe du monde 2026, Hervé Renard s'apprête à retrouver la Côte d'Ivoire. Selon plusieurs médias, dont RMC Sport, le technicien français sera officiellement nommé sélectionneur des Éléphants ce mercredi. Onze ans après avoir conduit la Côte d'Ivoire à son deuxième sacre continental lors de la CAN 2015, Renard succédera à Emerse Faé. Il prendra les commandes d'une génération prometteuse, emmenée notamment par Amad Diallo, Yan Diomandé et Christ Inao Oulaï, avec en ligne de mire la CAN 2027 et les qualifications pour le Mondial 2030. Son retour devrait être officialisé avant même l'élection du nouveau président de la Fédération ivoirienne de football (FIF), prévue le 12 septembre. Les modalités de son contrat n'ont, en revanche, pas encore été dévoilées. Cette nomination met fin aux spéculations qui entouraient l'avenir d'Hervé Renard. L'Algérie, en quête d'un successeur à Vladimir Petkovic, figurait parmi les sélections intéressées, tout comme le Sénégal, où Patrick Vieira apparaît désormais comme le principal favori pour prendre les rênes des Lions de la Teranga. L'Afrique du Sud et la Corée du Sud auraient également manifesté leur intérêt pour le technicien français. items.title: L’héritage !
items.description: Le 4 août 1983 a marqué l’avènement de la Révolution démocratique et populaire (RDP) conduite par le capitaine Thomas Sankara et ses compagnons, à la faveur d’un coup d’Etat ayant porté le Conseil national de la révolution (CNR) à la tête du pays. Il y a 43 ans, la gouvernance de la Haute-Volta d’alors affichait une volonté de rupture avec les anciens modèles de développement, en plaçant au cœur de son action, la souveraineté nationale, la justice sociale, la mobilisation populaire et la dignité du peuple burkinabè. Un an plus tard, le 4 août 1984, la Haute-Volta devenait officiellement le Burkina Faso, pays des Hommes intègres, consacrant ainsi une nouvelle identité nationale fondée sur les valeurs d’intégrité, de patriotisme et de responsabilité collective. La RDP a profondément marqué le pays par une série de réformes économiques, sociales, politiques et culturelles. Les campagnes nationales de vaccination, la construction d’écoles et de dispensaires, la promotion de la femme, la lutte contre la corruption, la réforme agraire, la recherche de l’autosuffisance alimentaire, l’appel à une gouvernance sobre et vertueuse ainsi que la volonté de réduire la dépendance extérieure ont constitué les principaux axes de la Révolution. La vision de la RDP et de son leader, le capitaine Thomas Sankara reposait sur la conviction que le développement du Burkina Faso devait être porté d’abord par les Burkinabè eux-mêmes, grâce au travail, à la discipline, à la solidarité et à la valorisation des ressources nationales. 43 ans après, cette période est plus que d’actualité. En effet, la Révolution progressiste populaire (RPP), conduite par le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, implémente, elle aussi, un projet centré sur la souveraineté, la transformation économique et la mobilisation des forces nationales. Dans leurs orientations, la RPP met en avant le renforcement de la production agricole, la transformation locale des matières premières, le développement d’infrastructures, la valorisation de la culture nationale ainsi que la promotion d’une économie davantage fondée sur les capacités endogènes. Les initiatives telles que Faso Mêbo traduisent cette volonté de faire du travail, de l’engagement citoyen et de la participation populaire des leviers essentiels de la construction de la Patrie. A cela s’ajoutent les initiatives visant à atteindre l’autosuffisance alimentaire (Offensive agropastorale et halieutique), à encourager la consommation des produits locaux, à soutenir les unités de transformation, à renforcer les infrastructures publiques et à consolider les fondements d’une économie plus résiliente face aux chocs extérieurs. La RPP s’inscrit ainsi dans une continuité de valeurs avec l’héritage de la RDP. Il s’agit de l’affirmation de la souveraineté nationale, l’autosuffisance alimentaire, le travail, la discipline, le développement endogène et la culture de la confiance des Burkinabè en leurs propres capacités. Cette dynamique s’inscrit toutefois dans un contexte particulièrement exigeant. Le Burkina Faso poursuit simultanément ses efforts de développement tout en faisant face à la menace terroriste. Malgré ces contraintes, des avancées significatives sont enregistrées dans tous les secteurs, notamment ceux de l’agriculture, des infrastructures, de la santé, de l’éducation, de la mobilisation des recettes et de la reconquête du territoire nationale et de l’autorité de l’Etat. La commémoration du 43e anniversaire de la Révolution démocratique et populaire rappelle que malgré les différences de contexte et de méthode entre les époques, l’ambition de bâtir un Burkina Faso souverain, prospère et maître de son destin est le même. Pour y arriver, les Burkinabè d’aujourd’hui sont appelés à devenir les héritiers de ces idéaux de patriotisme, d’intégrité et de responsabilité par le travail, l’unité et l’engagement citoyen. Jean-Marie TOE
